why: ONE expectation table for the capability policy, asserted by BOTH implementations:
(resolveCapabilitiesFromManifest). They are separate npm packages and cannot import
each other, so the Convex copy carries an 'EXACT MIRROR' comment and nothing ever
checked it. This file is the check: a divergence reddens one suite.
The manifest is SYNTHETIC on purpose. The shipped one cannot express the case that
matters — a capability declared for a version we have never benched — because every
real minVersion sits at or below maxValidated. On every other input, freezing at the
validated profile and failing open give the same answer, which is exactly why the
`historyCap` sits BELOW the floor: a capability first seen in a generation the floor
has since retired (0.92.0 raised the OpenClaw floor to 2026.8.2 over entries dating
from 2026.5.19). It discriminates the two floor rules: below the floor, nothing at
all; an unknown version gets every capability AT OR BELOW the floor, not only those

cases.name: mid-range: everything at or below the live version
exactly maxValidated is NOT beyond, and unbenched stays off
BEYOND maxValidated: frozen at the validated profile — this is the case that discriminates freeze from fail-open, and `unbenchedCap: false` is the whole point
far beyond: still the validated profile, never more
below the floor: nothing (the version clears no minVersion)
below the floor yet above an older capability's minVersion: STILL nothing — the floor retires the whole generation, not only what it lacked
unparseable version: CONSERVATIVE floor, and never the beyond flag
a provider with no published range: zero capabilities
